Consult Summary:
- Adult male with sudden-onset, persistent central chest pressure (7/10) with shortness of breath, light-headedness, nausea, and left arm/shoulder radiation; high concern for cardiac etiology. Emergency ambulance arranged for urgent hospital assessment.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Central chest discomfort/pressure “like someone sitting on my chest,” persistent.
- Onset/duration: Began suddenly a few hours prior to consult; constant since onset; currently unchanged (7/10).
- Context: Initially stated onset while digging in the garden. Later also stated he had been relaxing/watching TV before symptoms (conflict noted).
- Character/location/radiation: Midline chest pressure; radiates to left shoulder/arm; not to head; not to back.
- Associated symptoms: Shortness of breath, light-headedness, nausea (no vomiting), recent exertional dyspnea with stairs/hills.
- Other symptoms: Reports calf pain and leg swelling “often.”
- Pertinent negatives: No dysphagia or difficulty drinking; no problems “going to the loo”; no back radiation; no head radiation.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Triggered around physical activity (gardening) per initial report; no clear relieving factors reported.
- Recent intake: No food or drink earlier that morning.

Past Medical History:
- Hypertension (no current treatment documented).
- Hypercholesterolemia (no current treatment documented).
- Functional status: Limits daily activities due to dyspnea with exertion (stairs, uphill).

Medications:
- Current medications: None reported.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Social History:
- Tobacco: Smokes (quantity/frequency not documented).
- Lives with wife.
- Activities: Gardens about every other week; currently limits activity due to exertional symptoms.

Family History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Examination findings: Not recorded (telehealth).

Investigations:
- None completed at time of consult.
- Emergency services/ambulance arranged; paramedics to assess vitals and cardiac/respiratory status en route.

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - Working diagnosis: Suspected acute coronary syndrome (ACS) given classic ischemic features and risk factors. Pulmonary embolism (PE) also considered due to dyspnea and history of calf pain/leg swelling.

- DDx Integration (brief):
  - Acute Coronary Syndrome (high likelihood): Exertional central chest pressure, persistent >2 hours, left arm radiation, dyspnea, light-headedness, nausea; risk factors (HTN, hyperlipidemia, smoking). Opposing: No objective data yet (ECG/troponin not available).
  - Pulmonary Embolism (medium likelihood): Dyspnea/light-headedness with calf pain and leg swelling. Opposing: Chest pressure quality and left arm radiation more typical of ACS; no pleuritic pain or hemoptysis reported.
  - Musculoskeletal chest wall pain (low likelihood): Temporal association with activity possible. Opposing: Central pressure with arm radiation and systemic symptoms not typical.

- Issue 1: Acute central chest pressure with dyspnea, nausea; concern for ACS
  - Plan:
    - Emergency ambulance to patient’s address (initiated during call).
    - Advise patient to remain calm, sit/rest, and sip water as needed while awaiting paramedics.
    - Avoid taking any medications prior to assessment (per clinician advice).
    - Paramedics to perform urgent assessment (vitals, monitoring) and transport to hospital for immediate evaluation of heart and lungs.
    - Anticipated prompt assessment by hospital consultant on arrival.
    - Clinician to arrange follow-up after hospital evaluation.

- Issue 2: Dyspnea on exertion; reduced exercise tolerance
  - Plan:
    - Communicate to paramedics and hospital team as part of acute workup to assess for cardiac ischemia or alternative cardiopulmonary causes.
    - Further management deferred to in-hospital evaluation.

- Issue 3: Calf pain and leg swelling (intermittent)
  - Plan:
    - Communicate to paramedics/hospital due to potential thromboembolic risk (PE consideration).
    - Further diagnostic approach to be determined in hospital.

- General plan items:
  - Patient informed to involve wife for transport preparation; remain on the line until paramedics arrive.
  - Follow-up telehealth appointment to be arranged post-hospital visit.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected: Allergies not documented; detailed smoking history (amount/pack-years) not documented; no vitals or physical exam; no medication reconciliation beyond “none.”
- Conflicts: Onset context inconsistent—patient reported both gardening at onset and relaxing/watching TV before onset (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Some incomplete/overlapping responses; minor conversational ambiguities.
